headline: Compare both values and shape
statement: Given roots p and q of two binary trees, determine whether their node values and structure are identical. The trainer represents a tree as a level-order array, with null marking a missing child.
intuition: Matching values alone cannot prove that trees match: a left child and a right child occupy different positions. Compare paired nodes at the same position. If a position exists in only one tree, or its values differ, the entire answer is false.
approach: Start a stack with the pair of roots.
Skip a pair of absent nodes; reject when exactly one is absent.
Compare present node values, then push the corresponding left and right child pairs.
correctness: Every stack pair refers to the same structural position in both trees. Each mismatch is decisive. If no mismatch exists after all pairs are processed, every position is absent in both trees or has equal values, which is exactly tree equality.
bruteForce: Serialize both trees including missing-child markers and compare the serialized strings. This also works in O(n + m), but builds full representations instead of stopping immediately on a mismatch.

complexity.explanation: n and m are the node counts of the two trees; h is their maximum height. At most every corresponding node/null position is inspected before a mismatch. The depth-first stack stores deferred sibling pairs along a path, using O(h) auxiliary space.

pitfalls: Do not compare only traversal values: preserve missing-child positions.
An absent node and a present node must be unequal even if other values match.
